title: Orchard rollout brief and annotated ticker - Jul 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope
This doc captures the lightweight evening handoff checklist, 3-hour rollout ticker, and annotated release notes for Orchard (adaptive-batching v2). Orchard is a serving/runtime-level improvement that changes request coalescing behavior and batch sizing heuristics. The goal: reduce median token cost by ~12% while keeping 99th percentile latency within current SLO. This is a staged rollout (hosted + dedicated) with a Private deployment patch schedule to follow.

Audience
Primary: release engineering, serving-runtime, infra-SRE, product (hosted-api), on-call operators. Secondary: solutions engineering and customer success for high-touch customers.

Overview of the plan (short)
- Rollout window: evening quiet window starting 22:00 PDT on 2026-07-15 (low traffic).
- Canary cohorts: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100%. 3h planned ramp (staged holds at each step).
- Rollback thresholds: throttle or revert if latency p99 increases by >150ms relative to baseline for 10m, or error rate increase >0.5% absolute, or token cost regression >8% on observed traffic.
- Fallback: automatic policy in the Console to route to batcher-v1 or lower-quantized variant if memory pressure or OOMs observed.

Preflight (72–24h out) checklist
- [ ] Merge and green: all PRs merged; PRs linked above. Verify CI perf artifacts present. (Owners: Liam/Diego)
- [ ] Benchmarks: microbench for typical seq lengths (64/256/1024) uploaded to perf-store and compared to baseline. (Owner: Wei)
- [ ] Capacity check: Dedicated pool capacity verified for 1.2x expected burst; autoscaler config reviewed. (Owner: infra-eng)
- [ ] Telemetry hooks: ensure new batch metrics (batch-size-histogram, coalesce-latency) are present in observability and dashboards. (Owner: observability)
- [ ] Rollout policy stub in Console created and pre-reviewed. Policy ID: rollout-policy/orchard-v2 (attach before handoff).
- [ ] Customer-impact list: CS has list of customers with strict lat SLO and is notified of tentative window.
- [ ] Runbook: this doc uploaded and shared; emergency revert playbook linked.

Evening-of quick pre-launch (T-60 to T-10)
- T-60m: Confirm all autoscaling signals green and recent deploys within baseline. Slack channel #release-orchard opened and pinned. On-call for release engineering and SRE present.
- T-45m: Run smoke generator against staging: 1k requests across length distribution; validate outputs against golden set. (Owner: Maya)
- T-30m: Sanity dashboard snapshot (baseline latency, error rate, token cost). Save screenshots to the release thread.
- T-15m: Final sign-off via thumbs in the thread from owners (serving-runtime, infra, obs, product). If any veto, abort.
- T-10m: Canary traffic rule in Console primed (0.5%). Confirm fallback routes present and tested in dry-run.

Ticker and ramp plan (annotated)
- Stage 0: 0.5% (Duration: 15m)
  - Objectives: validate no immediate regressions, ensure batch-size histogram shows expected shift, KV cache usage stable.
  - Checks every 3m: p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, batch-size median, memory headroom.
  - Exit on success: move to Stage 1.
  - Fail/warn thresholds: p99 > +120ms for 3 consecutive checks or 5xx increases by >0.2%.

- Stage 1: 2% (Duration: 20m)
  - Objectives: see scaling behavior when batcher sees more concurrent requests, observe batching tails.
  - Add check: inference worker queue lengths and kernel queue times.
  - If memory climbs rapidly or OOM-like GC spikes, trigger rollback.

- Stage 2: 10% (Duration: 30m)
  - Objectives: validate throughput improvements and early cost signals.
  - Check cost-sampler telemetry and token accounting vs baseline cohort.
  - Manual spot-checks: run 3 targeted eval prompts from eval-suite to detect output degradation.

- Stage 3: 30% (Duration: 40m)
  - Objectives: confirm reliability at production-like scale; look for regional divergence in behavior.
  - Start targeted smoke against EU region to confirm cross-region parity (if applicable).

- Stage 4: 100% (Ramp to completion, monitored for 1h)
  - Objectives: full-environment validation and 1hr stability window.
  - Post-commit: create release note draft and close the runbook checklist.

Rollback and mitigation matrix (quick)
- Symptom: p99 jump >150ms for 10m -> Action: immediate throttle (50%) then rollback to pre-release model variant if persists >15m. Notify #oncall and product-ops.
- Symptom: sudden increase in 5xx or OOMs -> Action: instant rollback to previous routing policy. SRE to repro locally with trace logs.
- Symptom: token cost increases unexpectedly without latency improvement -> Action: pause rollout, compare batch histograms and sampling logs, may revert.

Operator console commands (cheat sheet)
- Activate policy: Console -> Rollouts -> rollout-policy/orchard-v2 -> Set cohort 0.5%
- Force fallback route: Console -> Routing -> create override -> target=pool:batcher-v1 -> priority=high
- Snapshot telemetry: observability -> Dashboards -> Orchard-Canary -> Export CSV

Nightwatch and 24h post-rollout tasks
- 0–1h: intensive watch (every 5m checks) by release team.
- 1–6h: hour-by-hour check-ins on Slack; SRE to watch error-traces.
- 6–24h: quiet watch with automated alerts. Capture any escalation triggers.
- Day+1: morning retro quick sync (30m) to capture immediate follow-ups and any config drift.
- Day+3: collect perf sampling from perf-store and compare to baseline; if any drift, open an investigation ticket.

Release notes (annotated draft)
Title: Orchard (adaptive-batching v2) — staged rollout
Highlights:
- Smarter coalescing for short- and mid-length sequences; expected cost reduction of ~12% median token cost.
- Tuned batch sizing to reduce tail latency regressions.
- No API surface change; rollout is routing-only.
Known limitations:
- Observed slight increase in batching variance for long-sequence (>1024) tails; addressed by a follow-up kernel scheduling tweak scheduled next sprint.
- Private on-prem bundles require a small config flip (batch-window-ms) — documented in Private-deploy README.

Action items left / TODOs
- [ ] Finalize Private deployment pack and checklist (Owner: Diego).
- [ ] Add automated smoke that exercises fallback route in CI (Owner: Liam).
- [ ] Update customer-facing release note page and CS email template (Owner: Ava).
- [ ] Run full quality eval (100 prompt set) after 24h at 100% traffic to ensure no model drift.

Open questions / discussion notes
- Should we open a limited early opt-in for a couple enterprise customers for earlier validation? (Pros: real traffic; Cons: support risk).
- Is the 3-hour ramp too aggressive for weekend windows? Suggest: switch to 6-hour ramp if any regional concurrency concerns.

Contacts and escalation
- Release lead: Maya Patel (primary) — slack: @maya, phone: +1-415-555-0123
- Serving runtime owner: Liam Chen — slack: @liamc
- Infra SRE: Wei Zhang — slack: @weiz
- Observability: Ava Thompson — slack: @avath
- Pager: SRE rotation — follow on-call roster (link in Confluence)

Appendix: useful artifacts
- Perf comparisons: perf-store/orchard/2026-07-10 vs baseline
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/orchard/pull/214 (perf artifacts attached)
- Revert PR template: github.com/redwood-inference/orchard/pull/legacy-revert-template

Notes to self (working)
- Keep annotated ticker short and keep staff focused on 3 metrics: p99 latency, 5xx rate, batch-size median. Everything else is noise for the first 60m.
- If we see a minor blip at Stage 2, prefer a short hold (10–15m) and deeper triage rather than automatic rollback.
- Remind CS to check top 10 customers for redlines tomorrow morning.

End of draft.

-- Maya
